Yes/no. Centrifugal force isn't a real force although it can be modeled as one. Centripetal force is higher at the equator but this plays into gravity which is relatively constant over the surface of the earth with some allowance for the earth not being a perfect sphere. Gravity pulls you toward the earth which acts in the same direction of centripetal acceleration (objects moving in a circular path accelerate toward the center of rotation). The force required to maintain the circular path is the centripetal force. Since the centripetal acceleration and gravity act in the same direction there is less apparent gravity where the centripetal acceleration is greater (at the equator due to the larger circular path with the same angular velocity).
